name: Hukumina
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct (Buru area); only Holle wordlists (Stokhof 1982) and survey atlases in Glottolog; no descriptive phonology exists that would state stress.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 2000. Defining speech communities on Buru Island: a look at both linguistic and non-linguistic factors. In C.E. Grimes (ed.), Spices from the East: papers in languages of eastern Indonesia, 73-103. Pacific Linguistics 503.
sources.note: Sec. 7.4.3: 'The language of Hukumina is very distinct from Buru in intonation, lexicon and sound correspondences' -- no stress location.
sources.venue: Spices from the East: papers in languages of eastern Indonesia

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 1995. Digging for the roots of language death in eastern Indonesia: the cases of Kayeli and Hukumina. Paper, 69th LSA Annual Meeting, New Orleans. ERIC ED384231 (precursor of Grimes 2009 in Florey ed.).
sources.note: Sound-correspondence and morphology comparison of Buru/Kayeli/Hukumina; stress mentioned only for Kayeli (enclitics extrametrical, 'not affecting penultimate stress on the root') and Buru; nothing on Hukumina stress; author notes he obtained 'very little reliable data' from the one Hukumina speaker.
sources.venue: Paper, 69th LSA Annual Meeting, New Orleans

sources.citation: LexiRumah 3.0 CLDF GitHub lessersunda/lexirumah-data) and ABVD (lexibank/abvd)
sources.note: Checked for a Hukumina lect/wordlist with stress marking: neither database contains Hukumina.
Nothing; stub with classification and extinction date only.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 2009. Digging for the roots of language death in eastern Indonesia: the cases of Kayeli and Hukumina. In M. Florey (ed.), Endangered Languages of Austronesia, 73-89. Oxford University Press.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.note: This work describes Kayeli (the only language given a stress statement); Hukumina is treated for sound correspondences and morphology only. No statement of Hukumina stress, accent or tone anywhere in the paper; the only Hukumina material is a handful of cognate forms (reflexes of *k, *s, *g, subject prefix g-ino) from one ~80-year-old semi-speaker in 1989. Nothing usable for a stress or tone entry. Published version of the 1995 LSA paper; may carry slightly expanded Hukumina data, though the precursor has no stress statement.

sources.citation: Taber, Mark (ed.) 1996. Atlas bahasa tanah Maluku. Ambon: Pusat Pengkajian dan Pengembangan Maluku, Universitas Pattimura / SIL.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.locator: Apendiks Dua, 'Bahasa dan Dialek yang tidak Tersenarai dalam Atlas', printed p. 126; index entries 'Hukumina, 126' and 'Bambaa, 126'
sources.note: The atlas does not list Hukumina among its languages; it appears only in Appendix Two (languages and dialects not covered), with one sentence: an 80-year-old speaker was reported in north-west Buru in 1989 (C. Grimes, pers. comm.), also known as Bambaa. No word list, no phonology, no stress/accent/tone statement. The atlas as a whole excludes stress: introduction, printed p. xi (p. 13): 'Data yang disajikan sudah dianalisis oleh para linguis SIL dan lazim digunakan dalam bentuk ortografis. Karena itu gejala-gejala fonetis seperti tekanan kata dan epentesis tidak disertakan di sini.' (phone Gl…

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 1991. The Buru language of Eastern Indonesia. PhD thesis, Australian National University. (hdl 1885/10925; scanned PDF, no text; scanned of pp.3-14 and 46-53 = printed pp.26-33)
sources.note: p.28 (sec. 4.1): Hukumina 'phonology (both synchronic and diachronic), morphology, stress patterns and intonation contours are strikingly different from Buru, Kayeli, Sula, Ambelau, and the languages indigenous to Ambon' -- mentions stress but does NOT state where it falls. (Phonology chapter 5.2 is on Buru stress, penultimate; not Hukumina.)

sources.citation: Stokhof, W.A.L. (ed.) 1982. Holle lists: vocabularies in languages of Indonesia Vol.3/4: Central Moluccas: Ambon (II), Buru, Nusa Laut, Saparua. Pacific Linguistics D-50. Hukumina = list 55b (NBG 1896), pp.63-76.
sources.note: Nothing. 'General information' gives only basic data (list 55b, 1896); wordlist diacritics (a-grave, i/o-macron, e-breve) are Holle vowel-quality/schwa marks per the Vol.1 conventions, not stress marks.

sources.citation: Stokhof, W.A.L. (ed.) 1980. Holle lists: vocabularies in languages of Indonesia Vol.1: Introductory volume. Pacific Linguistics D-17.
sources.note: Transcription key pp.76-77: a-grave = Dutch 'man' [short a], i-macron = Dutch 'vier' [i], e-breve = schwa; the questionnaire's stress questions (16-17) belong to the 1931 edition only, so the 1896 Hukumina list carries no stress information.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. 1989. Hukumina field notes and recordings (Masarete-Kayeli, Buru, May 1989), unpublished; possibly held by the author / SIL Indonesia or an archive (PARADISEC/OLAC could not be reached by automated download).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only first-hand Hukumina data ever collected by a linguist; Grimes 1991:28 says the stress patterns are 'strikingly different' from Buru/Kayeli, so his notes are the only place a stress location could be recorded.
